- When sentiment is negative (especially >2 consecutive negative values), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true outcome mean over 3+ consecutive days, apply downward bias adjustment of 1–3% per day.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, expect mean reversion toward 30-day moving average; adjust forecast to align with that.  
- If true outcome shows early downward trend (first 5–7 days), reduce forecasted peak by 5–10% to avoid premature overreaction.  
- When sentiment history includes multiple negative spikes, model should not overcorrect upward — cap forecast rise to 5% above recent high.
